message: Created 'Three-Month Mobile App Launch Plan' (Project plan) with 5 sections.
plan_reasoning: A project plan is the best fit because the request sets a fixed launch timeline and team size, requiring coordinated scope, ownership, milestones, and release controls. The sections move from defining the MVP and responsibilities to delivery, validation, and launch readiness.
assumptions: The three-month schedule means 12 calendar weeks, starting when the team is assembled and ending with a public launch.
The goal is to launch a minimum viable product (MVP), not a feature-complete long-term product.
The app will be built for iOS and Android using a shared cross-platform codebase unless product or technical constraints require otherwise.
The five-person team includes a product manager, designer, two engineers, and a QA/release lead; team members may share operational responsibilities.
Branding, core product requirements, and access to any required backend or third-party services will be available early in the project.

task_list.goal: Define the target users, launch objectives, success measures, supported platforms, and the features included in the initial release; explicitly defer nonessential features.
Assign responsibilities across the five-person team, establish decision-making and stakeholder review, and set a two-week sprint cadence with regular demos.
Sequence discovery and design, technical setup, core implementation, integration, stabilization, and launch preparation into week-based milestones with clear deliverables.
Plan functional, usability, device, and regression testing; define acceptance criteria, app-store submission requirements, analytics, support readiness, and launch approval.
Track schedule and technical risks, external dependencies, mitigation owners, status reporting, and contingency options that protect the launch date without compromising essential quality.
